definition: Self-reinforcing means strengthening itself so that each round makes the next more likely.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word self-reinforcing. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know self-reinforcing should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Confidence at the free-throw line is self-reinforcing; each make steadies the hands for the next.
Recurring is the weaker fact — a recurring bill merely comes back; a self-reinforcing one comes back bigger because of the last round.
Runaway goes further than self-reinforcing: a self-reinforcing loop still creeps, gathering strength turn by turn, while a runaway process has snapped every brake.

Snowballing is the informal picture of a self-reinforcing process: a rolling mass growing bigger with every turn, the avalanche already in view. It belongs in headlines and conversation; self-reinforcing is the analyst's term, precise about the mechanism — output feeding back in as input.

Compounding is the accountant's version of self-reinforcing growth: adding gains on top of previous gains, the way interest earns interest. It lives among quantities and rates. Self-reinforcing is broader and causal — each round strengthens the conditions for the next, whether anything is being counted or not.

Self-reinforcing means strengthening itself so that each round makes the next more likely.

Watch a hillside pasture and you can see why every cattle path is self-reinforcing: hooves wear the grass to bare dirt, rain finds the bare line and softens it, and soft ground pulls the next day's herd into exactly the same groove.
Within a few seasons the path is a trench no cow chose and no cow can avoid.
Self-reinforcing is the precise label because each round strengthens the conditions for the next — the loop's output becomes its own input, and the effect grows.
A merely repeated event lacks this: a weekly market recurs without deepening.
The trench is different; every pass makes the following pass more certain.
Self-reinforcing is the analyst's word for feedback loops that grow — panics, streaks, ruts, booms.
Its unit-mate self-perpetuating claims only continuation: a process that keeps itself going.
When the loop also gains strength each round, self-reinforcing is the sharper choice; when it merely never needs outside fuel, say self-perpetuating.

Rangeland ecologists describe a dry hillside as a system that can tip.
Grass holds soil; soil holds water; water grows grass.
Lose a little grass, and the loop runs the other way.
Each rain now strips soil the roots no longer hold, so less water soaks in, so less grass returns the following year.
The degradation is self-reinforcing: every round of loss makes the next round of loss easier.
That is why crews reseed after a single bad season instead of waiting -- once the feedback settles in, no one planting grass can outpace it.
